comparator.name: European Studies
comparator.sourceNotes: The current official UvA study-programme page and 2026–27 Course Catalogue establish a 180-EC, three-year European Studies bachelor. The shared first year is 60 EC: 36 EC of European history, integration, democracy, identity and culture plus four 6-EC modern-language proficiency modules. In years 2 and 3 students take one 48-EC major, Philosophy of the Humanities (6 EC), 24 EC of programme-related electives, 30 EC of free choice and a 12-EC bachelor thesis. The first-listed European Culture major is selected as the neutral route before considering UCR fit. The aggregate major and open choice spaces are retained without inventing internal courses.

alternatives.distinctnessRationale: Compared with the closest match, this route replaces extensive economics, law, international relations and historical-institutional study with media, rhetoric, social psychology, cultural production, entrepreneurship and advanced communication. It therefore changes both the disciplinary mix and the object of study from European governance to cultural identity and representation.

alternatives.concept: Concentrates the named European Law and European Politics directions around EU law, comparative constitutional law, human rights, international justice, political institutions, public argument and social equality. Economics remains supporting context rather than the programme’s organizing field.

progressionAssessment.rationale: No UCR course in this alternative carries a formal prerequisite except the courses that require GOSGATE102 (GOSLAWJ212, GOSLAWJ213, GOSLAWJ312) and BENGATE102 (BENECON211, BENECON212, BENECON312, BENECON311); GOSGATE102 is scheduled in semester 1 and BENGATE102 in semester 2, each before every course that depends on it. Personal & Professional Development is scheduled in semester 2, within Year 1. Introductory Year-1 courses (Law Society & Justice, Introduction to Political Philosophy, Foundations of Comparative Politics, Introduction to Economics) are concentrated in semester 1, and level-3 advanced work (Public Economics, Comparative Constitutional Law's prerequisite chain, European Union Politics, Persuasive Communication, Econometrics, Peace & Conflict, Foundations of European Union Law) is concentrated in semesters 4-6, so foundational training precedes advanced work. Where an advisory continuation exists in the course evidence, it is honoured: Research Methods & Statistics (semester 2) precedes the more advanced Econometrics (semester 6); The Art of Rhetorical Communication (semester 3) precedes the more advanced Persuasive Communication (semester 5); and Theory of International Relations (semester 2) precedes the more advanced European Union Politics (semester 5) and Peace & Conflict (semester 6). Every course is offered in its assigned semester under the fixed Fall 2026 cohort schedule.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The broad closest match covers the programme-defining study of European integration, politics, history, identity and political economy. European Culture/History and European Law/Politics/Economics support two coherent, feasible and pairwise distinct additional curricula. East European Studies lacks enough region-specific UCR depth for another defensible programme. Production stops at the maximum of three alternatives.

Both support sustained advanced cultural analysis of representation, identity and public meaning.
Both provide philosophical analysis of values, arguments and the foundations of humanistic inquiry.

UvA requires four modern-language proficiency modules. UCR has no equivalent language sequence, so those components remain unmatched rather than being replaced by general linguistics or intercultural courses.

UvA combines a shared European Studies core, language sequence and one named 48-EC major. UCR distributes related work across a student-designed interdisciplinary Liberal Arts and Sciences curriculum.
